newsitem.title: USA: Ala. Power sees state law withstanding suit.
newsitem.headline: Ala. Power sees state law withstanding suit.

text.p: Southern Co's Alabama Power Co expects a state electric law to withstand a legal challenge mounted earlier this week by a power marketer and two consumer groups, a company spokesman said Wednesday.
"We're very confident this law will stand up to the challenge," said Alabama Power spokesman Dave Rickey.

Monday, American Energy Solutions, Alabama Electric Consumers Coalition and Citizens for a Sound Economy filed a lawsuit with the federal district court against Alabama Power and three Alabama Public Service Commissioners.

"There is no guarantee whatsoever," Rickey said, adding the law simply set forth a process for the commission to review how the company may recoup from assets that become "stranded" in the move to a deregulated power market.
"The burden of proof is on the utility to show how much (stranded assets) are going to cost," he said.
Alabama Power's stranded costs are estimated at $200 million, according to studies by some industry analysts.
Alabama Power is the state's only investor-owned utility, providing electricity to 1.2 million customers.
Rickey said the state law does not prevent a customer from switching from Alabama Power to other electricity providers.
Alabama's lawmakers will likely reintroduce a bill, which stalled last year, to allow consumers to select their power suppliers.
